title: Sonodynamic Therapy for the Treatment of Glioblastoma Multiforme in a Mouse Model Using a Portable Benchtop Focused Ultrasound System
protocol: Perform intracranial tumor implantation according to a previously published report.
Quantify the tumor size in each mouse noninvasively using an in vivo luminescence imaging system prior to treatment.
Divide mice into comparable subgroups for treatment based on imaging quantification.
Weigh out 200 mg/kg mouse weight of 5-ALA under ambient light.
Dissolve the total amount of 5-ALA in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to make a 60 mg/mL solution.
Sterilize all equipment before use.
Inject the proper amount of 5-ALA solution into each animal intraperitoneally.
Leave animals for 3 hours to metabolize 5-ALA.
Fill a reservoir with deionized (DI) water.
Attach Flow in and Flow out tubes to the ultrasonic degasser.
Plug in the degasser, turn on, and run for 45 minutes.
Pour newly degassed DI water into an airtight sealed container.
Place ultrasound gel into a conical tube.
Spin the conical tube containing gel at 160 x g for 5 min to remove air.
Connect the MRgFUS system using the wiring diagram.
Power on the desktop computer, monitor, MRgFUS platform, oscilloscope, and amplifier.
Connect all cables to their correct locations.
Attach the transducer to the MRgFUS platform via BNC and coaxial cables.
Connect the impedance matching box to the appropriate wires.
Open the AUREUS application on the desktop computer.
Select Connect All Hardware in the AUREUS application.
Verify that all components are communicating with the software.
Unscrew the bottom screw from the phantom.
Fill the phantom cavity with deionized and degassed water until it overflows.
Replace the bottom screw after filling.
Place the phantom in its corresponding MRI bed location.
Insert the MRI bed into the MRI cradle in its designated slot.
Place the MRI cradle in its corresponding location in the MRI scanner.
Adjust the cradle so that the phantom MRI bed can slide into the MRI bore without obstructions.
Mark this location for future replication.
Take an MRI scan of the phantom using settings from Table 1.
Remove the cradle from the magnet bore but keep it on the scanner.
Remove the MRI bed containing the phantom from the cradle.
Place the bed with the phantom onto the MRgFUS system by sliding the peg into its correct slot.
Slot the registration tip onto the magnetic slots on the transducer arm so that it points downward toward the phantom.
Choose Select a New Home Position on the software.
Select Jog Mode On to begin guided focused finding.
Use the left, right, up, down, page up, and page down keys to manually move the transducer arm in all directions.
Adjust the pointer manually in all three dimensions until the tip of the pointer touches the middle of the cross pattern on top of the phantom.
Download the phantom MRI images to the computer.
Place the MRI images in a folder in the chosen directory.
Load the MRI images into the software by selecting Load Phantom Images.
Scroll through axial phantom slices via the mouse scroll bar.
Adjust brightness by clicking and holding on the image, then moving the mouse up or down.
Click on the middle of the phantom where there is a clear circle with three dark holes.
Drag the red circle until it matches the diameter and circumference of the phantom.
Save this position as 'home position' by clicking Set L/R, A/P, and S/I.
Click Jog Mode Off.
Remove the registration tip from the transducer arm.
Select Exit Focus Finding to confirm the home position.
Complete the initialization sequence.
Anesthetize the mouse using an isoflurane-O2 gas mixture in an induction chamber.
Set the gas flow rate to 1.0 mL/min and the vaporizer to 2.0% for anesthesia induction.
Keep the mouse in the chamber for 3-5 minutes until fully anesthetized.
Assess the animal for adequate sedation by pinching the toe.
Apply an ophthalmic ointment to the eyes to avoid dryness of the corneas.
Monitor the anesthesia depth throughout the procedure.
Inject the mouse with 40 µL of gadolinium contrast agent through the tail vein.
Remove any hair obstructing the scalp above the skull using a hair removal cream and an electronic shaver.
Connect the inlet tube of the MRI bed to a source of isoflurane for anesthesia induction.
Set the gas flow rate to 1.0 mL/min and the vaporizer to 2.0% for anesthesia induction.
Connect the outlet tube to a charcoal filter canister for anesthesia absorption.
Place the nose cone piece into its slot as shown.
Slide the bite bar through the bite bar holes in both the nose cone and at the end of the bed, with the bite guard end hovering over the open well in the MRI bed.
Place the animal on the MRI bed with its ears lined up with the stereotactic ear bar holes.
Latch the animal's teeth through the bite guard to keep it in place.
Slide the nose cone forward so that it is over top of the animal's snout to provide a steady stream of anesthesia.
Slide the ear bars through the holes on both sides of the MRI bed and raise the animal's head until both ear bars can fit into the mouse's ear canals.
Ensure that the animal is in a comfortable position.
Screw in the MRI-compatible screws to lock in both ear bars, the nose cone, and the bite bar.
Place the MRI bed on a warm heat pad to maintain body temperature.
Attach the inlet and outlet anesthesia tubes to the corresponding tubes in the MRI machine.
Slide the MRI cradle containing the animal into the MRI bore.
Perform a localizer scan to locate the animal brain.
Conduct a post-contrast T1-weighted MRI scan covering the entire brain using settings from Table 2.
Export MRI scans as uncompressed DICOM files for each slice.
Remove the animal from the MRI cradle after scanning.
Place the animal on the platform by slotting the bed into its corresponding pegs.
Connect the inlet tube of the MRI bed to a source of isoflurane with a gas flow rate of 1.0 mL/min and vaporizer set at 2.0% for anesthesia maintenance.
Connect the outlet tube to a charcoal filter canister for anesthesia absorption.
Transfer DICOM files to the computer and place them in the main working directory of the current study.
Turn on Jog Mode in the software by clicking Guided Focus Finding and then Jog Mode On.
Place a dab of centrifuged ultrasound gel on the animal's head, covering the entire scalp above the skull.
Pour DI and degassed water into the water bath up to 80%.
Slot the water bath onto its corresponding columns on the platform.
Lower the water bath until the bottom membrane touches the ultrasound gel on the animal's head.
Ensure that the ultrasound gel covers the entire head of the animal without air bubbles between the gel and the mouse's scalp.
Submerge the ultrasound transducer into the water bath, ensuring no air bubbles form on the transducer surface.
Lower the transducer arm using Jog Mode Down toward the partly submerged transducer.
Couple the transducer by aligning magnetic slots while keeping the transducer surface submerged.
Turn off Jog Mode.
Exit Focused Finding as done during the initialization step.
Confirm the home position as done before.
Go to the treatment tab.
Upload post-contrast T1-weighted MRI files by clicking the folder icon in the top middle of the screen.
Select the folder containing the DICOM files previously uploaded to the computer.
Open the selected folder.
Select either Burst or Continuous Wave mode in the Sonication Mode tab.
Enter burst length, burst period, and number of periods if using Burst mode.
Enter sonication duration for continuous wave mode (120 s).
Click on the target icon to select the proper locations on the MRI slice where the FUS focal region is aimed.
A light red square with a red circle will appear at each selected location.
Enter the 3D coordinates of the focal regions in the table.
Enter the power level for each focal spot in the last column of the table.
Click on each focal spot in the table to confirm and highlight the coordinates.
The corresponding focal region on the image will turn blue upon confirmation.
Select Motion Test in the software to ensure all focal regions are accessible.
Adjust focal regions if an error occurs during the motion test.
Once ready, select Begin Sonication to start the sonication protocol.
After finishing, uncouple the transducer from the arm and remove the water bath.
Wipe off ultrasound gel from the animal's scalp.
Unscrew bite and ear bars, then remove the animal from the MRI bed.
Place the animal on a warm pad until it wakes up from anesthesia.
Return the animal to its cage upon waking.
Repeat the protocol for subsequent animals starting from section 6.
Clean all surfaces touched by animals with 70% ethanol after treatment.
Quit out of the software and shut down each piece of equipment.
Repeat the IVIS protocol for bioluminescence measurement 24 hours post-treatment.
Perform follow-up MRI scans using the same settings from step 6.4.
Compare the mean grayscale intensity of the tumor region using contrast-enhanced scans.
Calculate the total volume covered by the contrast agent in the tumor region.
Determine differences in tumor volume pre- and post-treatment based on the analysis.
